extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, patent practitioners, and third-party reexamination requesters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting and responding to ex parte reexamination proceedings: when to order/rely on prior art, how to draft Office actions, timing and extension rules, and treatment of claims and evidence under MPEP and relevant CFR/statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) — mere reinterpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination request that merely provides a new interpretation of a reference already previously relied upon or actually discussed by the Office does not create a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other information in a reference (e.g., textbook material) actually teaches what is required by the claims, it may be appropriate to rely on that information to order/conduct reexamination; mere re-interpretation of an already-discussed reference is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination based on a previously-discussed reference when prior art status established
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner previously discussed a reference but did not reject or maintained rejection based on mistaken belief the reference did not qualify as prior art, a reexamination request explaining how/why the reference actually qualifies as prior art may justify reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of justificatory showings: (i) verify the date of the reference; (ii) undermine sufficiency of a declaration filed under 37 CFR 1.131; (iii) explain the correct filing date accorded a claim. Case cited: Heinl v. Godici.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language prior art — need for complete/accurate translation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign-language prior art reference was cited/discussed in prior prosecution but never completely and accurately translated into English during original prosecution, a reexamination request explaining why a more complete and accurate translation actually teaches what is required by the claims may justify reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portola Packaging does not prohibit reexamination in such circumstances; focus on whether translation now shows teachings required by claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative references — repetitiveness disqualifies reexamination if merely reiterative
rubrics_metrics.description: A cumulative reference that substantially reiterates verbatim the teachings of a reference previously relied upon or discussed may be prohibited from forming the basis of reexamination if it is merely repetitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such truly repetitive references are expected to be rare because most references present additional information or present it differently even if on the same subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices required to comply with In re Portola Packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution of an ongoing reexamination is terminated or a rejection withdrawn to comply with In re Portola Packaging, specific notice language must be used in the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate or Office action withdrawing the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact prescribed wording indicating termination/withdrawal based on In re Portola Packaging and that no patentability determination has been made in the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata and collateral estoppel treatment in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims finally held invalid by a Federal Court (after all appeals) will be withdrawn from consideration and not reexamined; collateral estoppel may be applied where the court decision applies in some respects to claims being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2242 and § 2286 for policy when a Federal Court decision on the merits exists for the patent under reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's duty under 37 CFR 1.104 — thorough study and investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up a patent in reexamination, the examiner shall make a thorough study of the file and thorough investigation of available prior art related to the claimed invention; examination shall be complete with respect to statutes, rules, patentability, and matters of form unless indicated otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes high-level thoroughness expectations for the examiner's work in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action content — notification of reasons for adverse action
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant (or patent owner and requester in reexamination) will be notified of the examiner's action; reasons for any adverse action or objections/requirements will be stated in an Office action and relevant information/references will be provided to aid judgment on continuing prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions must give sufficient information/useful references to allow the patent owner/requester to judge propriety of continuing prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978. Any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared at national examination upon written request and payment of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTO does not require such a report for claiming a later refund; procedural note on searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action — permissible limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's action will be complete as to all matters, except where appropriate to limit action due to misjoinder of invention, fundamental defects, and the like; matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may focus action on substantive defects as appropriate and defer form issues until allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejection — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, or not patentable as claimed, the claims (or those considered unpatentable) will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline: non-patentable claims must be rejected; follow statutory/guidance grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections for novelty/obviousness — cite best references and explain pertinency
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his/her command. When a reference is complex or shows inventions other than that claimed, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable and the pertinency of each reference must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must make clear which parts of references are relied upon and why they are pertinent to the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and examiner's knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant or patent owner in reexamination, and may rely upon facts within his/her knowledge (permitted by paragraph (d)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions in the file and official knowledge can support rejections, subject to the requirements for specificity and support for asserted facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f),(g) in 103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned by the same person/organization or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person/organization at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key ownership/assignment exception limits use of certain types of prior art in obviousness rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver preclusion by published statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an original application or reissue application naming an inventor will be rejected as precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed and the statutory invention registration waived that subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-part test: subject matter must be same and waiver in the statutory invention registration must have occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of references — required identification details
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing domestic patents, state numbers, dates, and names of patentees; for domestic patent application publications give publication number, date, and names of applicants; for foreign published apps/patents state nationality/country, numbers, dates, and patentee names and furnish data necessary to identify the documents. For parts of foreign documents, identify particular pages/sheets. For printed publications give author, title, date, pages/plates, place of publication, or where a copy can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sufficient detail to enable the patent owner/patent practitioner to identify and obtain cited references and the specific portions relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections based on employee personal knowledge — affidavit support
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an Office employee, the data shall be as specific as possible and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee, which is subject to contradiction or explanation by applicant affidavits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specificity and availability of employee affidavit are required when relying on such internal factual knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be set forth if unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record of prosecution as a whole does not make clear his/her reasons for allowing a claim, the examiner may set forth such reasoning in an Office action or separate communication, and the applicant/patent owner may file a statement commenting on those reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons should be incorporated into actions rejecting other claims or be provided as a separate communication; failure by the examiner to respond to comments does not carry implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: First ex parte action — primary action to establish issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's first ex parte action on the merits should be the primary action to establish the issues between examiner and patent owner in reexamination; it should be sufficiently focused and definitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At issuance of first action, patent owner has had opportunity to file statement/amendment and requester to reply. First action should caution the patent owner that a complete response is needed because next action is expected to be final; warn that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced and amendments after final must include a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule on submissions responding to Office action (Form paragraph 22.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure full consideration of any amendments, affidavits/declarations, or other documents as evidence of patentability, such documents must be submitted in response to the Office action; submissions after the next Office action (intended to be final) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116 and 37 CFR 41.33.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes timing: submit evidence in response to the action where it will be considered; late submissions face stricter rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims — treatment when base patent claim unamended and canceled
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unamended base patent claim (a claim as it appears in the patent) has been rejected or canceled, any claim directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be confirmed or allowed if the dependent claim is otherwise allowable; do not object/reject dependent claim merely because it depends on a rejected/canceled patent claim, and do not require rewriting dependent claim in independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because original patent claim numbers are preserved, canceled base claim content remains in the printed patent and is read as part of the dependent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims on new base claims — indefiniteness/rewriting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new base claim (one not appearing in the patent) has been canceled, a claim depending on it should be rejected as indefinite. If a new base claim or an amended patent claim is rejected, a dependent claim should be objected to (if otherwise patentable) and require rewriting the dependent claim in independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly introduced base claims do not enjoy the same protective treatment as original patent base claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch timing (35 U.S.C. 305) — first action timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination proceedings must be conducted with special dispatch; the examiner's first action on the merits should be completed within 1 month of the filing date of the requester's reply (37 CFR 1.535) or within 1 month of the patent owner's statement (37 CFR 1.530) if no requester. Mailing of the first action should occur within 6 weeks after the appropriate filing or due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes accelerated internal timing goals; litigation-involved reexams have priority over other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of first Office action in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Office action should be so complete that the second Office action can properly be made final; it must clearly set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to the claims, respond to the substance of each argument raised by patent owner/requester, and indicate reasons why claims are patentable when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First action must be thorough because of reexamination finality and patent owner inability to file a continuation; treat inappropriate arguments per 37 CFR 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title change procedure in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally title need not change during reexamination; if change is necessary, notify patent owner early to provide an amendment. If all claims are found patentable and Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate has been or will be mailed, title change by examiner may only be by formal Examiner's Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification and proper procedure required for title changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory periods for response in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period of 2 months will be set for response to Office actions in reexaminations, except where reexamination results from a court order or litigation is stayed for purposes of reexamination — then shortened period set at 1 month. Note: the 1-month policy does NOT apply to the 2-month period for filing a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 (set by 35 U.S.C. 304).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different shortened response strings depending on litigation context; statutory periods governed by statute where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and copying of Office actions — third-party requester notification
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions in a third-party requester ex parte reexamination will have a copy mailed to the third-party requester. Use transmittal form PTOL-465 for providing copies to third-party requester(s) and additional partial patent owners; the first patent owner's address is printed, and forms coordinate mailing copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural practice for ensuring proper service and record keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time in ex parte reexamination — 37 CFR 1.550(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for taking any action by a patent owner will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; any request must be filed on or before the due date and must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g). Mere filing of a request does not effect an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extension will be considered only after decision to grant/deny reexamination is mailed; requests before that decision will be denied. Certificate of mailing/transmission and Express Mail procedures may be used to file extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability of 37 CFR 1.136 in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) and (b) are NOT applicable to ex parte reexamination proceedings under any circumstances because 1.136 applies only to an 'application' and ex parte reexamination involves neither an 'application' nor an 'applicant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time in reexamination must be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c), not 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on granting extensions — first vs subsequent requests
rubrics_metrics.description: First requests for extensions of statutory time periods will be granted for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time (usually 1 month). Second or subsequent requests or requests for more than 1 month will be granted only in extraordinary situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation considers whether sufficient cause shown and the statute's 'special dispatch' requirement; factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior favors grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions for third-party requester reply under 37 CFR 1.535
rubrics_metrics.description: The time period for filing a third-party requester reply under 37 CFR 1.535 to the patent owner's statement (2 months from date of service) cannot be extended under any circumstances; statutory period is rigid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory periods cannot be waived or extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic 1-month extension upon filing first timely response after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a timely first response to a final rejection having a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the shortened period for an additional month, which will be granted (but total period may not exceed 6 months from date of final action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This automatic 1-month extension applies only to the first response to a final rejection and not after filing a Notice of Appeal. Timely first response includes informal or unsigned responses; purpose is to avoid appeals merely to gain time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action practice for amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners will normally complete a response to an amendment after final rejection within 5 days; if advisory action cannot be mailed in time for patent owner to consider examiner's position before termination, additional time may be granted and set forth in the advisory Office action, but reply period cannot exceed 6 months from mailing date of final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory action form PTOL-467 used; if patent owner files further amendment during extended period it must place reexamination in condition for allowance or prosecution will be terminated absent timely appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to submit affidavits after final — potential denial and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: When patent owners request extension to submit an affidavit after final rejection, granting such extension is without prejudice to the examiner's ability to question why the affidavit is now necessary and why it was not earlier presented; if showing insufficient, examiner may deny entry of the affidavit notwithstanding the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of extension primarily keeps prosecution from terminating while allowing opportunity to present affidavit; admission of affidavits must comply with 37 CFR 1.113 and related rules; refusal to admit affidavit and related proceedings may follow.
